summary: Typosquat of ckcc-protocol exfiltrates wallet, SSH, AWS, and env secrets to webhook.site
details: On first require(), index.js reads installer-side secrets —.env,.npmrc, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_rsa|ed25519|ecdsa, ~/.config/solana/id.json, ~/.ethereum/keystore — and enumerates home dotdirectories for files matching wallet/key/secret/seed/mnemonic/keystore/private (plus.json/.pem), reading files under ~50KB. Contents are JSON-packed with os.hostname() and os.userInfo() and POSTed via https to webhook.site at path /5c5ad6cb-62df-4ea5-9dfb-2c447920ddc4. Execution is gated behind a hardcoded activation timestamp (Date.UTC(2026,7,6)) with an author comment stating the delay is intended to evade npm sandbox detection windows. The package name mimics the legitimate Coldcard ckcc-protocol library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
